fields.title: More accurate family relationships
fields.description: Legacy now keeps every person in an imported family tree separate, even when two people share the same name — so no one ends up with impossible parents. The Family view always opens centered on you, no searching required. If a tree you imported earlier looks off, open Family and choose "Looks off?" to rebuild it correctly from your original file.

fields.title: Exact dates from your family tree are preserved
fields.description: When you import a family tree, Legacy now keeps the exact dates it contains — so a birthday shows as "29 Mar 1971" instead of just "1971," on profiles, People cards, and the Family view. Deaths and marriage dates are kept too. When only a year is known, Legacy still shows the year, and it never guesses a date it doesn't have.

fields.title: Describe relationships the way they really were
fields.description: Relationships in Legacy are no longer just "spouse" or "parent." You can now choose from many types — spouse, former spouse, partner, fiancé, parent, step parent, adoptive parent, guardian, sibling, half sibling, friend, coworker, mentor, pastor, neighbor, and more — and set whether it's current, former, or estranged, along with when it started and ended and any notes. Add, edit, or remove relationships right from a person's profile. Not every parent comes from a marriage, and now Legacy can say so.

fields.title: Merge duplicate people into one
fields.description: If the same person shows up twice in your Legacy — say "Marvin Jenkins" and "Marvin Lynn Jenkins" — you can now merge them. Open a person's profile, choose "Merge with existing person," and pick who they really are. Everything moves to the surviving person: their stories, photos, media, places, relationships, milestones, quotes, and aliases. The duplicate disappears, nothing is left behind, and the old name still works in search.

fields.title: People opens on the family closest to you
fields.description: The People page now opens on the people who matter most — you, your parents, spouse, siblings, and children — instead of your entire list. A 'Browse all' link shows everyone, now neatly paged so even a large imported family stays fast, and search still finds anyone by name or nickname.

fields.title: Family View gets a profile panel and color-coded connections
fields.description: The Family view now shows a profile panel beside the tree: click anyone and their photo, dates, parents, spouse, children, and siblings appear on the right — each one clickable to move through the family — with a button to open their full profile. Relationship lines are now color-coded so the tree is easy to read at a glance: blue up to parents, green down to children, gold between spouses, and a dotted line for siblings, with a legend to match. Your own card is marked so you always know where you are.

fields.title: Family View now explores one person at a time
fields.description: The Family view now works the way a family tree should. Instead of showing your whole tree at once, it shows one person's immediate family — their parents above, spouse and siblings beside them, and children below — so it's easy to read at a glance. Click any relative and the tree re-centers on them; click the highlighted person to open their full profile. Search finds anyone in your whole family and brings them to the center, and the 🏠 Me button always returns to you. The Relationships page has also come to life, pointing to your Family view and showing what's coming next for friends, coworkers, mentors, and more.

fields.title: Family View now feels like a family tree
fields.description: The Family view now lays your family out as a proper tree: parents above, children below, siblings beside each other, and spouses together — so the generations are easy to read at a glance. It opens centered on you, and a new 🏠 Me button always brings you back home. You can also search your family by name or nickname and jump straight to anyone. Set who you are with 'This is me' on any person's profile.

fields.title: Family View — explore the people in your Legacy
fields.description: There's a new Family view in Legacy. It shows the people you've added — by hand, through your stories, or by importing a family tree — as an interactive tree you can pan, zoom, and drag. Each person appears as a card with their photo (or initials), name, and years, and tapping one opens their full profile: their stories, photos, places, life milestones, relationships, and more. If you imported a GEDCOM family tree, use 'Add to my family' on the import to bring those people and their marriages and children into the tree. It's not genealogy software — it's a warm window into everything Legacy knows about the people you love.

fields.title: Import your family tree (GEDCOM) — kept as genealogy, not stories
fields.description: You can now bring a family-tree file (GEDCOM, the standard genealogy export) into Legacy. Legacy recognizes it automatically and reads the people and families straight into dedicated genealogy review queues — with names, births, deaths, marriages and children preserved as structured records, never mashed into stories. As always, nothing enters your Legacy until you review it. And when Legacy isn't sure what a piece of a document is, it now sets it aside as 'Needs clarification' instead of guessing it's a story.

fields.title: Import understands your whole document, not just stories
fields.description: When you import a document into Legacy, it no longer assumes everything is a story. Legacy now reads each part and recognizes what it is — a story, a fact, a person, a place, a life milestone, a quote — and sorts them into review queues for you. Facts like 'I married on June 7, 1997' are kept as facts instead of being turned into stories. Your narratives still flow through the same review-and-confirm process, and nothing enters your Legacy until you approve it. One upload, intelligently organized.

fields.title: Cleaner, more readable story cards
fields.description: Your story cards in Legacy now put the title on a clean background at the top, with the photo shown large below it and the date underneath. The title is always easy to read — never sitting on top of the image. Stories without a photo yet show a short preview of their text instead, so every card looks tidy and consistent.

fields.title: One photo can belong to many memories
fields.description: Media is now fully reusable in Legacy. A photo you add while writing a story reliably stays attached to it — through saving, refreshing, and reopening. And from a photo's page you can now connect it to as many stories as you like: it shows every story it's part of (open any of them, or remove it from one without deleting the photo), the people and places it's connected to, and a searchable list of your other stories with helpful suggestions to add it to. Nothing is ever duplicated — the same picture simply enriches every memory it belongs to.

fields.title: Legacy suggests a title for your story
fields.description: One less thing to think about: if you haven't given your story a title when you tap Discover, Legacy now suggests a simple, natural one based on what you wrote — and you can edit it however you like before saving. If you've already written your own title, Legacy leaves it exactly as is. We also made sure your photos stay put: a picture you add to a story stays attached through saving, reloading, and reopening, and each story keeps a clean, readable tile with a consistent thumbnail. Nothing feels temporary, and nothing gets lost.

fields.title: See everything connected to your story
fields.description: After Legacy reads a story and you apply what it found, those people, places, milestones, photos, and moments no longer disappear — they stay visible in a tidy Connections panel beside your story. Each section shows a count and expands when you want detail, and everything is one tap away: a person opens their profile, a place opens its page (with an Open in Google Maps link when a location is known), a photo opens its detail. It all stays put when you reload the page, and your attached photos are always shown. Now it's obvious: Legacy found these things, you approved them, and they're a lasting part of the story.

fields.title: Legacy identifies the places you mention — using what it already knows
fields.description: When you mention a real place in a story, Legacy now identifies it as part of the same step where it reads your story — using the context it already has. If your story names a city, it uses that; if you already mentioned a nearby place, it uses that; and if you don't mention a location, it uses the home town in your Preferences. It shows you the official name and location, tells you why it chose that place, and marks it Verified or a Possible match. If it isn't sure, it simply says so and lets you keep your own wording — it never makes up an address. As always, nothing is saved until you confirm.

fields.title: Legacy figures out which place you meant
fields.description: When you mention a place in a story, Legacy is now much better at identifying the right one — because it uses what it already knows before searching. If your story names a city ("we were visiting Riverside, California"), it searches there. If you already mentioned another place nearby ("we left UT Medical Center and stopped at Nauti K's"), it understands the second place is near the first. And if you don't mention a location at all ("I stopped by Nauti K's after work"), it searches close to the home town in your Preferences. It shows you where it looked and marks a result as Verified or a Possible match, and you always confirm before anything is saved. The result: you rarely have to type a city or an address yourself.

fields.title: Legacy tidies your writing and finds the places you mention
fields.description: Telling a story just got easier. When you tap Discover, Legacy now quietly cleans up your writing first — fixing spelling, punctuation, and grammar and breaking up long paragraphs, without ever changing your words, voice, or meaning. You'll see a short note of what was tidied, and you can undo it in one tap to keep your original wording. Then, when you mention a real place like a restaurant or a church, Legacy helps identify the correct one so you don't have to type an address: it checks whether the place is already in your Legacy, recognizes personal spots like "Grandma's house" and offers to keep them as personal places, and looks up the name and location of public places for you to confirm. Nothing is ever changed automatically — you always review and choose before anything is saved.

fields.title: Legacy connects your existing photos to the story you're telling
fields.description: When you write a story, Legacy now also looks through the photos and media you've already added and gently suggests any that seem to belong with it — shown right in the panel with a thumbnail and an "already uploaded" tag. It's only a suggestion: nothing attaches until you say so, a photo can belong to as many stories as you like, and it's never moved or duplicated. So the picture of the farmhouse you uploaded last month can quietly find its way to the story about summers there.

fields.title: Legacy: tidy up your media, and a calmer Discovery panel
fields.description: A couple of small refinements to Legacy. You can now tidy your media the same forgiving way you handle stories: set a photo or clip aside to take it out of your library without deleting it, then either restore it or permanently delete it — with a clear confirmation so nothing disappears by accident. And when Legacy reads a story and shows you what it understood, those findings are now grouped into calm, collapsible sections — People, Places, Life, Time, Meaning, and Media — so the panel stays easy to scan even when there's a lot to review. Nothing is ever hidden or applied on its own; you still choose what to keep.

fields.title: Legacy now listens, keeps photos with their stories, and welcomes your written life
fields.description: Legacy just got easier and more natural to use. You can now tap Talk and simply speak — your words are transcribed live as you go, and everything works exactly the same whether you spoke a memory or typed it. Photos and media now belong with the story you're writing: drag them straight onto a memory (or browse to add several at once), see them previewed, and remove any before you save — nothing is ever duplicated. The home page is clearer too: "Add Photos & Media" is where your photos, video, and audio go, while a new "Import your life" brings in memoirs, journals, and ChatGPT or Claude exports and turns them into stories. And if a file lands in the wrong place, Legacy gently points you to the right one instead of showing an error.

fields.title: Your Chief of Staff keeps thinking even if you leave the page
fields.description: Ask a question in chat and you no longer have to sit and wait on the same screen for the answer. If you switch tabs, move to another part of the app, or even refresh the page while your Chief of Staff is still working, the answer keeps being prepared in the background instead of being thrown away. When you come back to the conversation, the completed reply is already waiting for you — and if it's still being written, the chat reconnects and picks the response up live, the way you'd expect from a modern assistant. Your question and its reply are saved either way, so nothing gets lost to a stray tap or a reload.

fields.title: Your Executive Briefing now tells one clear story
fields.description: The Executive Briefing at the top of your dashboard used to occasionally contradict itself — for example showing a "Steady" status badge next to a headline that said you were slipping, or "All clear" right beside a real concern. We've added a single guiding read of your day: the status badge and the headline now come from the same underlying assessment, so they always agree. "All clear" only appears when there genuinely is nothing behind, anything still open today is surfaced as a concern, and a forward-looking risk (like "overload risk if this keeps up") never gets mislabelled as your "Biggest Opportunity" or quietly flips a stable day into a bad one. The result is one coherent narrative: a clear current state on top, with opportunities and risks supporting it underneath rather than fighting it.

fields.title: Your daily rhythms stay completable all the way to midnight
fields.description: A rhythm is no longer "too late" just because its scheduled time has passed. If something was set for 7:00 AM and you get to it at 10:00 PM, it's still fully available today — you can tick it off, undo it, or use the group "Complete" button for a whole batch of medications or supplements. Those mass-complete buttons no longer disappear once a block moves into the past; everything scheduled for today stays actionable right up to midnight. The scheduled time still shapes your ordering and reminders, and items you haven't gotten to yet are now labelled "Behind — still available today" instead of anything that feels like failure. Tomorrow's items remain previewed as coming up, and past days stay locked as history.

fields.title: Tell your Chief of Staff you're skipping a routine — and it actually sticks
fields.description: You can now skip a routine item for the day just by saying so in chat. Tell your Chief of Staff "I'm not showering today", "skip journal tonight", or "not doing my stretches today, starting fresh tomorrow" and it will mark that routine as skipped for today — a real change, not just a polite reply. The skipped item immediately drops out of your check-ins, so when you ask for a check-in it won't keep listing something you've already decided not to do. It's only for today: the routine returns as normal tomorrow. Skipping is never treated as completing, and if your assistant can't find the routine you mentioned, it tells you honestly instead of pretending it did something.

fields.title: Your Projected A1C (GMI) now always tells you where it stands
fields.description: If you track glucose, the Projected A1C (GMI) on your Mission card will no longer quietly disappear. It now always shows you exactly where things stand. When your data is fresh and dense, you see the number with a "High confidence" note. When your CGM sync is running a little behind, you still see the estimate, marked with a tilde and "Waiting for recent glucose sync". If there genuinely isn't enough recent data yet, you'll see an honest "Need more glucose history" prompt instead of a guessed figure — and if your monitor is connected but readings haven't come through, it says "Waiting for glucose sync" so you know it's a sync delay, not you. In the rare case the estimate can't be calculated, it says "Unavailable" rather than vanishing. On a health-focused mission, this metric is also given priority so it's never crowded out by other signals.

fields.title: Projected A1C is now an industry-standard estimate — and more dependable
fields.description: We refined the Projected A1C on your Mission card so it matches the standard method used across continuous glucose monitoring. The number you see is now the recognised GMI (Glucose Management Indicator) estimate calculated straight from the simple average of your glucose readings — the same approach the major CGM systems use — with no extra adjustments quietly changing the figure. It's labelled "Projected A1C (GMI)" with a note that it's based on your CGM history, not a laboratory A1C. We also made it more reliable: if your glucose sync is a few days behind, the estimate no longer disappears — it stays visible, with an honest confidence level. When there genuinely isn't enough recent data to be sure, you'll see a gentle prompt to sync more rather than a guessed number. Trend still drives the encouragement: a falling A1C is always framed as the progress it is.

fields.title: Your Mission card is now tappable — and quietly tracks your health trajectory
fields.description: The signals on your Primary Mission card are now actionable. When a driver has a meaningful next step — your workouts, your activity, your sleep, your journal, your nutrition — you can tap it to jump straight to that part of the app. The cues are subtle on purpose: a gentle highlight and a small arrow on hover, never a loud button. Automated metrics like glucose open their insights view rather than a manual log, because they're already tracked for you. The whole card still opens your mission when you tap anywhere else. There's also a new Projected A1C signal for anyone tracking glucose. It reads your existing glucose history and estimates your A1C trajectory, then places it in Helping momentum, Worth watching, or Needs attention based on the direction it's heading — because a number that's falling is encouraging even while it's still coming down. It only appears when there's enough recent, consistent data to be trustworthy; if the data is too sparse to be sure, it stays hidden rather than guessing. Nothing here is invented, and a falling trend is always framed as the progress it is.

fields.title: Make your Mission personal — add an image, links, and wins along the way
fields.description: Your Primary Mission is about something that matters to you, so the Mission card can now hold onto why. On a goal's page you'll find a new “Mission Inspiration” area: add a meaningful image (a finish line, a dream location, a wedding photo — whatever your mission is), write a short personal note about why it matters right now, and pin a few quick links you want close at hand, like a race website or an inspiration board. When you set an image, it shows up as a small, tasteful thumbnail on your dashboard Mission card, and your links appear as a compact “Mission Actions” row you can tap straight from the dashboard. There's also a lightweight “Wins Along the Way” section for the small victories worth remembering — your first 5K without stopping, two consistent weeks, a milestone that isn't on the formal plan. These wins are separate from your major milestones, so logging them celebrates progress without changing your goal's official tracking. Everything here is optional and entirely yours: nothing is invented, nothing is required, and the card stays clean if you'd rather keep it simple.

fields.title: Your Mission card now reads recovery fairly — and added a “Worth watching” lane
fields.description: The Mission card just got more truthful and more encouraging. First, it reads recovery fairly: around six hours of sleep is no longer treated as a failure. If you're rebuilding your health, training, and movement, that's enough to maintain momentum — so sleep in that range now shows as something to keep an eye on, not a red flag. Only genuinely thin recovery is flagged as needing attention. Second, the drivers strip went from a stark two-way split to three honest lanes: “Helping momentum” for what's genuinely working, a new amber “Worth watching” lane for the middle ground (sleep that's okay but could climb, nutrition that's tracked but not yet dialled in, movement that's happening but light), and “Needs attention” reserved only for what's really slipping. That middle lane matters: not everything is either a win or a problem, and the card now says so. The coaching line follows the same spirit — truthful and supportive, never fake positivity, and always grounded in the signals you actually track.

fields.title: Your Mission now understands movement, not just steps
fields.description: The Mission card used to judge your activity mostly by daily steps — which is unfair if walking is hard on you but you stay active through workouts, biking, pickleball or strength training. It now reads an adaptive Movement signal instead. It looks at the activity you actually track — structured workouts and their active minutes alongside your steps — and decides whether you're genuinely moving, not just whether you walked a lot. It also adapts to where your mission is: early on, consistency and conditioning count more than step volume, so staying active through workouts reads as momentum even on light-step days; later, as a mission shifts toward something like building running tolerance, daily activity volume starts to matter more again. The coaching line follows suit — if your movement is strong it credits you for staying active despite limitations rather than scolding low steps. As always it's honest: Movement only appears when you've tracked activity, and nothing is invented.

fields.title: Your Mission card now reads its own momentum
fields.description: Your Primary Mission card is no longer just a pretty progress ring — it now tells you, in plain language, how the mission is actually going. Using the signals you already track (workouts, sleep, steps, weight trend, journaling and nutrition) plus your real momentum trend, it settles on one honest state: Getting started, Building momentum, Improving, Maintaining, Slipping, or Needs attention. The ring centre shows that state as a word — BUILDING, MOMENTUM, ON TRACK, STEADY, RECOVER or REFOCUS — so an early "0 of 4 milestones" reads as a beginning, not a failure. The coaching line beneath it speaks to your real signals: if your training is consistent it says so; if nutrition isn't tracked yet, it names that as your next lever. And the drivers strip now splits into "Helping momentum" and "Needs attention," showing at most three of each, or "No major concerns" when nothing's slipping. Everything stays honest: a direction like Improving only appears when your real momentum is genuinely rising, never as a guess.

fields.title: Your Primary Mission, reimagined as a North Star
fields.description: The dashboard Mission card just became a hero. When you choose a Primary Mission, it now appears as a premium, motivating card built around a progress ring that shows how far you've come through your milestones — a real count like "2 of 5," never a made-up score. You'll see your current focus (your next milestone) and the date it's due, a "How things are going" panel that reads your real momentum trend, a days-remaining countdown, and a Key Drivers strip that surfaces the everyday signals behind your progress — weight, workouts, steps, sleep, journaling and nutrition — pulled straight from your own data, with anything you haven't tracked simply left out. There's also an optional "Why this matters" line drawn straight from your own words. You can give your mission a personal icon — a flag, a target, any emoji — by setting a Mission Icon on the goal, or simply by starting the goal's title with an emoji. Everything on the card is honest: if there's no data for a row, it stays hidden, and the card itself only appears once you've chosen a Primary Mission. It should feel like you're preparing for something meaningful.

fields.title: Choose your Primary Mission
fields.description: You can now pick one Goal as your Primary Mission — the single North Star you want front and centre. Open any active goal and tap ⭐ “Make this my Primary Mission.” That goal becomes the featured Mission card on your dashboard and the one your Chief of Staff coaches you toward, with a short momentum-aware nudge. Only one Primary Mission is active at a time, so choosing a new one steps the previous goal down automatically. This is your choice, not a guess: if you haven't selected a Primary Mission, no Mission card appears and your Chief of Staff stays quiet on it. You can clear it any time from the same goal.

fields.title: Experimental: Chief-of-Staff dashboard preview at /dashboard-v3/
fields.description: A brand-new, experimental dashboard is available alongside your regular dashboard. Visit /dashboard-v3/ to try it. The current dashboard at /dashboard/ is unchanged — nothing about your normal experience is affected. The preview is structured around a Chief-of-Staff briefing first, accountability second, and your checklist third. You'll see top life gauges with trend direction, an executive summary of what's going well and what needs attention, a single 'Focus Right Now' recommendation, per-domain accountability cards, and rhythm-based execution blocks (Morning, Day, Evening, Night) that expand and collapse around the time of day. Weather and water tiles are tucked into supporting roles instead of taking premium real estate. Everything you see is built from the same canonical data sources your assistant reads, so the dashboard and assistant cannot disagree. Try it, then let us know what you think.

fields.title: Action Center vocabulary: no more punitive "EXPIRED"
fields.description: The homepage Action Center used to mark everyday items — a 7 AM protein shake, morning measurements, a routine supplement — as "EXPIRED" the moment their scheduled window passed. That felt like a failure tracker. It's now aligned with the Recovery Contract: "recover forward, not punitive." Items past their optimal window show "BEHIND" instead — still visually de-emphasised, still completable from the homepage with one tap, just not labelled as gone. The stronger word "MISSED" is now reserved for genuinely time-locked commitments where the moment really is gone (a church service, a meeting, an appointment, a class). The recovery banner's aggregate count reads "X behind, Y past window" instead of "Y expired." Nothing about completion changes — if you do something later, you still complete it normally. The homepage now represents the living reality of your day, not a clock-enforcement scoreboard.

fields.title: Gospel reading plans now feel consistently guided
fields.description: Every day of every Gospel reading plan (Matthew, Mark, Luke, and John) now includes the full canonical structure: a Context section to ground the passage, three levels of Commentary (beginner, intermediate, advanced), a Reflection prompt, and your private Reflection entry. Previously some days in the John plan were missing Context or Commentary — not because the content didn't exist, but because the database loader couldn't update day entries once they were created. The loader is now content-authoritative, and a one-time refresh ensures every existing day in every gospel plan is brought up to the same standard. The John plan now feels as intentionally designed and spiritually rich as Matthew.

fields.title: Your Chief of Staff now understands what you're asking
fields.description: Ask 'What should I do right now?' and you get your next overdue task. Ask 'What is my biggest risk?' and you get the health or adherence issue most likely to compound. Ask 'What should I fix first?' and you get the most critical gap. Previously all three questions returned the exact same answer — now they route to three distinct decision handlers. 'What should I do' focuses on execution (overdue tasks and schedule). 'Biggest risk' evaluates medication adherence, health trends, and cross-domain patterns. 'Fix first' is a hybrid — critical risks override execution, but if nothing is critical, it falls back to the task list. Your Chief of Staff now thinks about the question, not just the data.

fields.title: Smarter next-action selection
fields.description: When you ask 'What should I do right now?', your Chief of Staff now picks the right specific action — not just the right category. Previously it would select 'Wake up' (an implied-done routine toggle) over 'Work on WLJ' (your actual anchor task) simply because Wake up had an earlier timestamp. Now it filters out status-toggle items you've obviously already done (like waking up, if you're interacting with the system), prioritizes explicit task commitments over routine maintenance toggles, and selects foundational items before flexible ones. The result: the single most impactful actionable item, every time.

fields.title: Your Chief of Staff now thinks about your day, not just your data
fields.description: Ask 'What should I do right now?' and your Chief of Staff will look at what's overdue, what's coming up in the next 90 minutes, and what daily commitments you haven't completed — in that order, before ever looking at trends or insights. Previously it might have said 'Plan an earlier wind-down tonight' while you had 5 overdue morning items. Now it says 'Start Wake up' and lists what else is behind. Signals and trends (sleep declining, nutrition low) only surface when there's nothing actionable on your schedule. The system now behaves like a disciplined operator managing your current day, not a strategist optimizing long-term numbers.

fields.title: Decisive next step, guaranteed
fields.description: Ask 'What should I do?', 'What is the biggest risk?', 'What's not working?', 'Help me decide', or 'What should I fix first?' — and your Chief of Staff will always lead with a single, specific next action, never a summary. The guarantee is built into the router and validator, not a request to the AI. Responses now start with 'Do this next:' or 'Your priority is:' on every decision question, always have exactly one action (no menus of options), and never start with 'End of day...' or 'Here's what happened today...'. Passive filler like 'keep logging' and 'continue tracking' is also rejected — active verbs only.

fields.title: One clear next step, every time
fields.description: Your Chief of Staff now produces exactly ONE primary action per response, with a direct prefix like 'Do this next:' or 'Your priority is:'. No more menus of options, no more 'you might consider' language. When multiple signals compete for attention, a strict priority order decides: Health risk beats foundational habits, which beats time-sensitive items, which beats optimization. And cross-domain patterns your Chief of Staff notices (sleep declining + workout intensity rising → recovery risk, for example) are now surfaced explicitly as reasoning — not buried inside individual signals. Direct, decisive, and always prioritized.

fields.title: Accurate adherence, sleep, and workout numbers — no more drift
fields.description: Your Chief of Staff was occasionally showing stale adherence percentages, sleep trends, and workout counts because the cached state only refreshed when you logged something new. On a quiet day, yesterday's numbers would linger. Now the medication, supplement, sleep, and workout rolling metrics are re-computed fresh on every chat turn, so the panel you see and the narrative your Chief of Staff reads will always agree. The labs trend-detection panel was also silently broken by a refactor — it's fixed and now shows your abnormal-lab history again.

fields.title: Disabled modules stay quiet
fields.description: If you've turned off a module (nutrition, health, or finance) your Chief of Staff will no longer fabricate insights about it. Previously a handful of insight rules used default values like '100% goal progress' or 'perfect medication adherence' whenever a domain was disabled — which meant users with a module off could still receive false-positive 'great job!' or 'watch out!' insights about things they don't even track. Five rules (motivation drift, overtraining risk, compliance risk, workout consistency, fasting consistency) now cleanly bail when their underlying domain is disabled. The nutrition and health summary views also respect the disabled state instead of showing empty data tiles.

fields.title: More accurate medication and adherence numbers
fields.description: A behind-the-scenes math bug was causing your Chief of Staff to see medication and supplement adherence at 100 times their real value — so a true 80% medication adherence was being reported to the AI as 8000% and a real 30% supplement rate looked like 3000%. That's been fixed everywhere your adherence numbers flow, which means insights, summaries, and recommendations about your medications and supplements will now reflect reality. A few other silently-dead insight rules (weight gain + missed medication correlation, body-fat rebound confirmation, medication line in the health summary) have also been reconnected to the right data so they actually fire when they should.

fields.title: Sharper trend detection across sleep, body comp, and workouts
fields.description: Your Chief of Staff can now see trends in data it was previously blind to. Sleep trends (increasing / decreasing / stable) are computed from your last 14 nights instead of always defaulting to 'stable' — meaning a run of short nights will actually surface in overtraining warnings and cross-domain insights. Body fat and waist measurements now show whether you're trending up or down over the last 30+ days. Workout recency is surfaced as 'days since last workout' so your Chief of Staff can spot gaps. Nothing changed in the UI directly — these are signals that flow into smarter insights and more accurate answers whenever you ask your Chief of Staff about recovery, fat loss, or training consistency.

fields.title: You'll always know what happened to your last request
fields.description: Every assistant reply now shows a clear status badge so you never have to wonder. Replies that completed in the background while you were on another tab show 'Completed while you were away' with a subtle amber border so they stand out from fresh responses. Failed requests show 'Couldn't finish — try again'. If you accidentally hit Send twice while your last request is still working, instead of a vague message you'll see a dedicated card showing exactly what you asked, how long ago you submitted it, and a 'View latest result' button you can tap to grab the answer the moment it's ready.

fields.title: Your request keeps working even when you navigate away
fields.description: Switching tabs, navigating to another page, or losing your connection no longer cancels what your Chief of Staff is working on. Requests now run to completion server-side and the result is saved the moment it's ready — so when you come back, the reply is already waiting for you in the chat. Your typed message is also saved as a draft on every keystroke, and is only cleared once the server confirms it received your request, so a failed send will never lose your text. For queries that depend on the page you're looking at (like 'save this' or 'add this to my list'), the page context is now captured the instant you hit Send — and if you navigate away before your Chief of Staff captured it, you'll get a clear 'I lost the context, can you bring that back?' message instead of a guess. Retries after a network blip no longer fall into unrelated flows.

fields.title: Clearer, safer confirmations before any change
fields.description: Before your Chief of Staff creates, updates, or deletes anything, you now see an explicit summary that spells out exactly what's about to happen. Every confirmation shows the action, a field-by-field breakdown of the details (Title, Day, Time, Repeats…), and a specific impact line with the magnitude of the change (for example, 'Moves this task 1 hour later' or 'Adds a new weekly entry to your calendar'). Updates now show both Before and After side-by-side so you can see exactly what's changing. Critical and Foundational items get a time-sensitivity warning. Instead of typing CONFIRM/CANCEL/EDIT, you now see three clearly colored pill buttons — Confirm (blue), Edit (gray), and Cancel (red) — that you can tap on mobile, click on desktop, or answer with plain words like 'yes', 'edit', or 'cancel'. If your Chief of Staff is missing information it needs, it now asks a clarifying question instead of rendering a vague confirmation.

fields.title: Ask 'What's my workout tomorrow?' and get a real answer
fields.description: Your Chief of Staff can now answer forward-looking questions about your scheduled workouts. Ask 'What is my workout tomorrow?', 'What's my next workout?', or 'What's planned for tomorrow?' and get a deterministic answer pulled directly from your active workout plan and weekly schedule — never a guess. If nothing is scheduled, it tells you so plainly instead of inventing a workout name. The same protection applies across every other domain (sleep, steps, weight, etc.) — forward-looking questions now route through the deterministic event pipeline instead of historical summaries.

fields.title: More accurate cross-domain insights
fields.description: Your Chief of Staff no longer claims that fasting or workouts have 'dropped' for areas you don't actually track. Cross-domain pattern detection now respects your enabled modules, so a disabled domain (like fasting) can never be correlated against an active one. Workout consistency also now uses your scheduled-plan adherence as the source of truth instead of a 30-day rolling ratio that under-reported highly consistent users after a vacation or rest week.

fields.title: Supplement Tracking
fields.description: Track your supplements alongside medications with the new Unified Intake System! Add supplements like creatine, vitamins, and fish oil with their own schedules and adherence tracking. Supplements appear in the Action Center with their own groups, and your Chief of Staff can distinguish between medications (critical) and supplements (optimization) when answering your questions. If you were tracking creatine under hydration, it has been automatically moved to the supplement system.

fields.title: Activity-Based Workouts
fields.description: You can now log duration-based activities like pickleball, walking, cycling, and more! Just tap 'Activity' on the workout form, pick your activity, enter the duration, and you're done. Activity workouts count toward your daily routine completion (10+ minutes required) and generate intelligent training load signals. Multiple short sessions in a day combine together.

fields.title: Stale DB Connection Recovery
fields.description: Improved error handling when database connections are temporarily interrupted. The app now recovers gracefully instead of showing raw error pages, and resumes normal operation automatically when connections restore.

fields.title: Behavioral Signals V3
fields.description: The behavioral signal system has been upgraded with grouped event presentation, adaptive dashboard cards, and feedback buttons. You'll see more relevant insights about your patterns — medication adherence, sleep recovery, activity momentum — and can give thumbs up/down to improve what gets surfaced.

fields.title: Dashboard: Physical Intelligence Coach
fields.description: A new coaching panel on your dashboard synthesizes health data across body composition, workout patterns, recovery signals, and nutrition into clear, actionable guidance. All analysis is deterministic — grounded in your actual data, not AI guesses.

fields.title: Execution Compliance Engine
fields.description: The system now tracks what you committed to vs. what you actually did across 6 domains: tasks, journal, workouts, medication, faith, and routines. Your dashboard shows a compliance summary that powers morning reconciliation and daily progress scoring.

fields.title: Hydration: Drink Type Tracking
fields.description: Water tracking just got smarter. You can now log 8 different drink types — water, coffee, tea, electrolytes, creatine, juice, milk, and more. Each drink has a hydration coefficient so your daily total reflects actual hydration impact (coffee counts as 90%, electrolytes as 105%). Quick-log buttons on your health dashboard let you tap to add common drinks instantly. If you're consistently taking creatine, your hydration goal automatically adjusts upward.

fields.title: Life Alignment Cockpit
fields.description: Your dashboard now opens with three visual dials showing how aligned you are across Faith, Health, and Work/Purpose. Each dial scores your 7-day consistency (0-100%), shows trend direction, and color-codes from red to green. Tap any dial to see the detailed breakdown — Bible reading days, prayer consistency, workout adherence, medication tracking, sleep quality, task completion, and milestone progress. The cockpit answers one question at a glance: Am I living aligned with what matters most?

fields.title: Chief of Staff: Smart Task Coaching
fields.description: Your Chief of Staff now understands your task workload in real time. She knows what's overdue, what's coming up, and how much progress you've made today. When you ask about your tasks or what to work on next, she gives you one clear action based on what matters most right now — personalized with your actual task names and time-aware based on your schedule.

fields.title: Chief of Staff: Health-Aware Coaching
fields.description: Your Chief of Staff now understands your health status in real time. When you ask about your health or daily focus, she leads with a single clear action based on what matters most right now — whether that's taking overdue medications, getting more sleep, or simply staying consistent. Her coaching is grounded in your actual data, never guessed.

fields.title: Health: Right Now Priority Summary
fields.description: Your Physical Health page now shows a compact 'Right Now' summary at the top with up to 4 priority items. Overdue medications appear first, followed by any vitals that need attention, then reassuring signals like normal blood pressure or strong sleep. Items are freshness-gated — stale readings are automatically suppressed so you only see what's current and relevant.

fields.title: Morning Check-In: Yesterday's Routines
fields.description: Each morning, your dashboard now shows any routine items from yesterday that weren't marked complete. For each item you can tap 'On Schedule' (did it on time), 'Later' (did it but late), or 'Skip'. This ensures your routine history stays accurate without extra effort — just answer once in the morning and you're done.

fields.title: Routines: Smarter Timing & Quick Actions
fields.description: Routine tracking now captures when you actually did an activity, not just when you tapped. New buttons let you mark items as 'Done at Scheduled Time' if you did them on time but logged later — no more false late marks. Each time section has bulk actions: Done All at Scheduled Time, Complete All, and Skip All. On-time items show green, late items show orange. Your routine signals and insights are now based on actual behavior, not click timing.

fields.title: Routines: Journal & Bible Auto-Complete
fields.description: Routine items now auto-complete across all activity types! Journaling and Bible reading join workouts in automatically marking your routine items as done when you log the actual activity. Your routine view shows exactly what completed each item — like "Completed via Back + Arms at 6:42 AM" for workouts, or "Completed via Journal Entry at 8:15 PM" for journaling. Your Chief of Staff now references your actual activities instead of generic completion flags.

fields.title: Routines: Auto-Complete from Workouts
fields.description: Workout routines now auto-complete when you log a workout! No more checking the same thing twice. The system tracks exactly which workout fulfilled the routine, uses your workout start time for on-time/late detection, and the first workout of the day wins. Activity-type routines show status-first language like "Completed via Workout at 6:42 AM" instead of a checkbox. You can set any routine item to Activity type in the routine editor to enable this behavior.

fields.title: Routines: Track Your Daily Habits
fields.description: A brand new Routines section lets you define and track daily recurring habits like morning prayer, exercise, or evening journaling. Routines are grouped by time of day (Morning, Afternoon, Evening, Nightly) with the current window highlighted. Check off items as you complete them throughout the day. If you had tasks marked as routines, use the migration tool to convert them to the new system.

fields.title: Navigation: All Domains Now Accessible
fields.description: People, Notes, and Brain Training are now accessible from the main navigation. People appears as a top-level item for managing contacts and relationships. Notes lets you capture and organize thoughts. Brain Training is available under Health for cognitive exercises.

fields.title: Interactive A/B/C Option Buttons in Chat
fields.description: When your Chief of Staff offers you choices (A, B, C, D), they now appear as tappable buttons instead of plain text. Pick your option with a single tap — no typing needed. This works for all conversational choices, not just confirmations. Options automatically highlight the recommended choice.

fields.title: Smart Dashboard: Next Action + Time-Aware Schedule
fields.description: The dashboard now tells you exactly what to do next. A new 'Next Action' panel highlights your most important pending item with smart priority (overdue first, then what's happening now, then next routine or medicine). Today's Schedule groups items into NOW, NEXT, and LATER sections. Medicine stacks only appear when relevant to the current time. Health metrics are compact chips instead of a large grid.

fields.title: Command Console: Smarter Execution
fields.description: The dashboard execution section is now a true daily command console. Completed routines compress into a compact strip so you focus on what's next. Medicine is grouped into stacks (Morning, Evening, Night) with one-tap completion. Tasks and calendar events merge into a single 'Today's Schedule' timeline. Every item title is a link to its source page. Insights only appear when they're meaningful — silence beats filler.

fields.title: Life Command Center: Execution Layer
fields.description: Dashboard V2 now answers 'What should I do right now?' The execution section is promoted to the top of the page with grouped routines, medicine, tasks, and calendar events — each with completion count badges. Items show which goal they contribute to. Routine rows include subtle engagement strength indicators. Goal gauge drivers now show real domain signals (workouts, weight trend, sleep avg, scripture reading). Sleep metric fixed from minutes to hours display. All 'streak' language replaced with consistency-oriented messaging.

fields.title: Life Command Center (Beta)
fields.description: A new experimental dashboard at /v2/ reimagined as your life command center. See goal momentum gauges showing how strongly you're moving toward each goal, a daily progress ring tracking routines, medicine, tasks, workouts, journaling, and faith. Complete daily actions inline without navigating away. Earn celebrations when you hit meaningful milestones — consistency patterns, goal progress, and more.

fields.title: Chief of Staff Responds Instantly to Health Questions
fields.description: Ask your Chief of Staff about your weight, workouts, sleep, glucose, medication, steps, blood pressure, or heart rate and she'll respond in under a second — no more waiting 15-30 seconds for simple status checks. Your Chief of Staff pulls your latest data directly from your tracked metrics and offers to dig deeper if you want analysis.

fields.title: Chief of Staff Checks In Throughout the Day
fields.description: Your Chief of Staff now reaches out at the right moments — morning medicine reminders, midday progress snapshots, afternoon non-negotiable nudges, and evening day-closing summaries. Your Chief of Staff respects your quiet hours and adapts to your timezone, so you'll hear from her when it actually matters.

fields.title: Chief of Staff Speaks More Naturally Now
fields.description: Your Chief of Staff's responses now feel more like a real conversation. Instead of robotic confirmations like '✓ Logged heart rate: 72 BPM', she says things like 'Got it — 72 BPM is logged.' Confirmation buttons now say 'Sounds good' and 'Never mind' instead of 'Confirm' and 'Cancel'. When your Chief of Staff can't find what you're looking for in one area, she'll check related areas too — ask to update a task that's actually a calendar event, and she'll point you in the right direction.

fields.title: AI Action Success Rate Monitoring
fields.description: The Operations Wall now tracks every AI action the Chief of Staff attempts — showing real-time success rates across 5-minute, 1-hour, and 24-hour windows. Blocked actions (learning mode, safety gates) are tracked separately from actual failures, so the health signal stays clean. Status thresholds automatically flag when failure rates cross warning or critical levels.

fields.title: Smarter Confirmation Flow with Quick-Tap Options
fields.description: When your Chief of Staff asks you to confirm an action (logging data, creating tasks, etc.), you now see clickable A/B/C option buttons instead of typing CONFIRM or CANCEL. Your Chief of Staff also learns your patterns over time — if you always confirm weight logs, she'll highlight that option first. After completing an action, you'll see a 'View it' link to jump straight to the relevant page. Behind the scenes, all pending actions are now durably stored for crash recovery, rate-limited to prevent accidental duplicates, and fully auditable.

fields.title: Smart Workout Inputs for Every Exercise Type
fields.description: Your workout tracker now adapts to how you actually exercise. Bodyweight exercises like push-ups and pull-ups show just a reps field (with an optional '+ Weight' toggle for weighted variations). Time-based exercises like Plank show a duration input in seconds. Weighted exercises keep the familiar weight + reps layout. Personal records now include 'Longest Hold' for time-based exercises, and training volume automatically accounts for your bodyweight on bodyweight movements. Templates remember your last duration for planks too.

fields.title: Chief of Staff Now Interprets Your Health Screenshots
fields.description: When you share a health screenshot from Apple Health, Fitbit, Garmin, or any health app, your Chief of Staff no longer just reads the numbers back to you. She now analyzes your sleep data through the Pattern Intelligence Engine — evaluating sleep duration, stage distribution, and cycle completion against clinical reference ranges. Your Chief of Staff connects findings to your personal context (wake time, fitness goals, health conditions) and gives you one clear, actionable recommendation. This is health reasoning, not just data recitation.

fields.title: Delete Recurring Tasks Completely
fields.description: You can now ask your Chief of Staff to delete an entire recurring task series — not just one instance. Say 'delete Approve Payroll completely' or 'stop this recurring task' and your Chief of Staff will ask whether you want to remove the whole series or just one occurrence. Once confirmed, all instances are removed and the task stops coming back. Your Chief of Staff also properly handles task deletion now instead of telling you to do it manually.

fields.title: Chief of Staff Now Trusts You When You Say It's Done
fields.description: When your Chief of Staff reminds you about something and you tell her you already did it, she now trusts your word — acknowledges it, stops reminding you, and moves on. No more repeated prompts after you've told her it's handled. She'll also offer to log it for you if you'd like, but won't do it automatically. This applies to all activities: journaling, workouts, medication, prayer, habits, and tasks.

fields.title: Chief of Staff Now Remembers Your Life Story
fields.description: Your Chief of Staff now permanently remembers important personal details you share in conversation — like family relationships, losses, milestones, and life circumstances. These facts are stored securely and used to make your Chief of Staff more emotionally aware and empathetic in future conversations. You never have to repeat yourself about the things that matter most.

fields.title: Non-Negotiable Task Commitments
fields.description: Tasks now support commitment levels: Optional, Important, and Non-Negotiable. Mark your most essential tasks as non-negotiable and your Chief of Staff will coach you if you start skipping them — gently at first, then with more awareness if it becomes a pattern. Skip streaks reset automatically after 7 days of no skips. You can also set commitment levels on your life goals.

fields.title: Pantry Storage Intelligence & Barcode Scanner
fields.description: Your pantry now organizes items by physical location — Fridge, Pantry, Freezer — with smart auto-classification. Scan any product barcode on the pantry page to instantly add items. Receipt processing now shows a real progress bar instead of a spinner, and won't get stuck thanks to improved error handling.

fields.title: Faster, Smarter Receipt Processing
fields.description: Receipt scanning just got a major upgrade: images are now compressed before processing (faster uploads), processing happens in the background so you're not waiting, duplicate receipts are automatically detected, and each receipt now shows a financial breakdown with subtotal, tax, and payment method.

fields.title: Skip Tasks You Didn't Do
fields.description: Tasks now support three states: pending, completed, and skipped. When you miss a workout or decide to pass on a task, mark it as skipped instead of leaving it overdue forever. Skipped tasks don't count as completed in your stats. For recurring tasks like daily workouts, skipping still generates the next occurrence. You can also ask the assistant to skip tasks for you.

fields.title: Receipt Photo Scanning
fields.description: Snap a photo of any receipt and the system automatically extracts items, classifies the receipt type (grocery, restaurant, or retail), and routes data to the right place — grocery items go to your Pantry, restaurant visits get logged in Health, and all purchases are tracked in Finance. You can review and edit detected items before confirming.

fields.title: Health Intelligence Dashboard
fields.description: See your body composition intelligence at a glance — fat loss phase, plateau risk, muscle preservation status, and fat loss quality now appear on your dashboard. Tap through to the full Health Intelligence page for trend charts, detailed explanations of what your numbers mean, risk warnings, and your scan history.

fields.title: Smarter Relationships Tile
fields.description: Your Relationships dashboard tile just got a lot smarter. It now shows a color-coded health score, switches between attention mode (who needs a call) and healthy mode (your anchor people and insights), and surfaces relationship patterns you might miss.

fields.title: Smarter Task & Habit Completion
fields.description: When you tell your Chief of Staff you finished something — like prayer time, Bible reading, or a workout — she now handles both sides automatically: logs the habit AND marks the task complete. She also knows your schedule in real time, so if you're chatting during workout time, she'll give you a friendly heads-up. And when she's not sure what you mean, she'll ask instead of guessing wrong.

fields.title: Email Your Medicine List
fields.description: Ask your Chief of Staff to email your medicine list — perfect for doctor visits. Just say "email me my medicine list" or "send my medicines to doc@example.com" and you'll receive a professional email with all your active medications, doses, schedules, prescribing doctors, and 30-day adherence stats for each medicine. Adherence is color-coded (green/yellow/red) so you can see consistency at a glance.

fields.title: Multi-Recipe Photo Detection & Prayer Awareness
fields.description: Cookbook pages with multiple recipes are now detected automatically — each recipe on the page becomes its own entry during bulk import. Also, your Chief of Staff now knows about your active prayer requests, answered prayers, and Bible reading progress, so you can ask faith-related questions in conversation.

fields.title: Expanded Relationship Types
fields.description: The relationship type dropdown now has 23 options instead of 7. You can now specify Father, Mother, Son, Daughter, Brother, Sister, Grandfather, Grandmother, and many more specific family relationships when editing a person.

fields.title: Bulk Recipe Photo Import
fields.description: Import up to 50 recipe photos at once. Upload your photos, and AI processes each one in the background — extracting titles, ingredients, instructions, and more. Review all extracted recipes on a single page with live progress tracking, then confirm individually or all at once. Find the new “Bulk Import” button on the Recipes page.

fields.title: People & Groups: New Tile Card Design
fields.description: The People list and Group detail pages now display contacts as visual tile cards with colored avatar initials (color-coded by relationship type), interaction counts, and time since last contact. Each card is clickable and highlights on hover. Multi-select, bulk actions, and group creation all work the same way with the new layout.

fields.title: Smarter Chief of Staff: Decisive Coaching with Quick Actions
fields.description: Your Chief of Staff just got a major intelligence upgrade. Morning briefings now feel like a natural conversation — you’ll hear about your wins, outstanding tasks, and the single most important thing to focus on, with quick A/B/C options to act immediately, schedule for later, or defer. CoS now automatically detects non-negotiables (medication timing, workout consistency, hard deadlines) and prioritizes them first. When you override a recommendation, CoS learns from your choice and adapts. Data discussions start with a sharp executive snapshot — type ‘Deep Dive’ anytime for the full strategic breakdown. And if drift is detected, CoS intervenes directly with a reset plan instead of waiting for you to ask.

fields.title: Smarter Morning Routine: Auto-Completion & Proactive Nudges
fields.description: Your morning routine just got smarter. Tasks now display in chronological order (Wake Up → Prayer → Bible Reading → Workout). When you interact with your Chief of Staff for the first time each day, your Wake Up task is automatically marked complete. Completing a Bible reading marks your Bible Reading task done. Logging a workout checks off your Workout task. Taking medication completes your Medicine task. Your Chief of Staff also proactively nudges you about upcoming activities and celebrates your accomplishments before mentioning what’s next.

fields.title: Share Up to 5 Images at Once with Chief of Staff
fields.description: You can now attach up to 5 images in a single CoS message — perfect for sharing health charts, InBody screenshots, or progress photos all at once. CoS analyzes every image together and gives you a combined, data-driven response with specific numbers and trends. Select multiple files from the picker (Cmd+click or Shift+click), or paste images one at a time.

fields.title: Context-Aware Help on Every Page
fields.description: The help button (?) now shows page-specific guidance everywhere in the app — Meals, Medical, Relationships, Billing, Capture, Notifications, Favorites, and more. 32 new help topics were added covering what each page does and how to use it. Previously, most pages showed generic navigation help instead of specific content.

fields.title: Import Contacts from Your Phone (iOS)
fields.description: Add contacts to WLJ directly from your phone's contact list. Tap 'Import from Phone' when adding a new person, pick a contact, and their name, phone number, and email are filled in automatically. No double-keying — you set the relationship type and notes after import. One contact at a time, fully intentional.

fields.title: @Mention Autocomplete Everywhere
fields.description: Type @ in any text field across the app — journal entries, tasks, prayers, goals, reflections, chat, and more — and a dropdown instantly suggests matching contacts and groups. Select with keyboard or click, and quickly create new contacts inline if someone isn't in your list yet.

fields.title: Calendar: Add Task Button & Time Display Fixes
fields.description: The Month view now has an "Add Task" button that takes you to the task form and brings you right back to the same month when you're done. We also fixed calendar event times that could display 1 hour off, and eliminated duplicate events that appeared when a recurring event overlapped with a manual entry.

fields.title: Contact Import from Phone
fields.description: Import contacts from your phone by uploading a vCard (.vcf) file. Supports exports from iPhone, Android, and Google Contacts. Automatically deduplicates against existing contacts and shows a clear summary of what was imported, skipped, or had errors.

fields.title: @Group Mentions
fields.description: Type @GroupName in journal entries or prayers to mention everyone in a group at once. Each member gets their own interaction record. The autocomplete dropdown now shows your groups with a people icon and member count, making it easy to tag entire groups.

fields.title: Smarter Task Matching & Time Range Support
fields.description: Your Chief of Staff is now much better at finding the right task when names overlap. Saying 'complete Workout' now correctly targets the task titled 'Workout' instead of also matching 'Post-Workout Stretch'. When multiple tasks match, you can pick by number or name, and your selection is resolved instantly without re-searching. You can also now schedule tasks with time ranges — saying 'add a task at 5pm to 6pm' captures both the start and end time.

fields.title: Recipe Photo Import — Scan Recipes with Your Camera
fields.description: Take a photo of any recipe — from a cookbook, recipe card, magazine, or handwritten note — and AI will extract the title, ingredients, instructions, cooking times, and more. Review and edit the extracted data before saving. The original photo is stored alongside your recipe for reference.

fields.title: Meal Intelligence — Setup Mode Now Shows What's Coming
fields.description: The Meal Intelligence setup experience now gives you a preview of the system's full power before you activate it. The setup dashboard shows a 'Kitchen Intelligence Initialization' hero with six capability tags (blood sugar protection, protein alignment, waste reduction, calendar awareness, grocery efficiency, family scaling), three locked preview cards showing exactly what activates next (optimized dinner score, expiration alert, grocery stats), and a 'Why This Matters' side panel. The setup wizard now opens with a preamble — 'You're 3 minutes away from activating a household optimization engine' — and each step uses capability-unlock language so you know what you're building toward.

fields.title: Relationship Insights Dashboard
fields.description: See how healthy your relational connections are at a glance. A new Insights page under People shows your Relational Health score (0–100), highlights people needing attention, reveals context balance across Journal, Tasks, Events, and Prayer, and identifies your relational anchors. A compact summary card on your Dashboard keeps the key numbers visible without leaving home.

fields.title: People & Relationship Intelligence
fields.description: A new People section lets you track the important relationships in your life. Add contacts, see interaction history across Journal, Tasks, Prayer, and Events, and use @mentions to tag people in your entries. Your Chief of Staff now has relationship awareness — it knows who matters most and when you last connected.

fields.title: Pantry Photo Intelligence — Scan Your Kitchen with AI
fields.description: Take photos of your fridge, pantry shelf, or freezer and let AI detect the food items inside. Each scan creates a session where you review and confirm detected items before they're added to your pantry. Track session history with confidence scores and monitor pantry freshness over time.

fields.title: Meal Intelligence — Your Kitchen Command Center
fields.description: A complete Meal Intelligence pillar is now live. Get personalized dinner suggestions scored against your pantry, nutrition goals, and dietary needs. Track your pantry inventory with confidence scoring, plan weekly meals with a calendar view, upload grocery receipts to auto-update your pantry, and explore recipes with nutrition breakdowns, gap analysis, and substitution suggestions. Access it all from the new Meals entry in the sidebar.

fields.title: Dynamic Search Across All Pages
fields.description: Search boxes throughout the app now auto-search as you type. After a brief pause, results update automatically — no need to press Enter or click Search. This applies to Tasks, Journal, Audio Capture, Admin Task List, and Notes. Focus stays in the search box after results load so you can keep refining your query.

fields.title: Chief of Staff Now Understands Follow-Up Requests
fields.description: Your Chief of Staff can now understand follow-up requests in conversation. When you say things like 'remove the other one', 'delete that event', or 'move it to tomorrow', CoS now uses conversation context to figure out exactly what you're referring to. Previously, these follow-up requests would fail because the system couldn't resolve references like 'the other one'. Calendar events also now automatically create a backing task, so everything on your calendar can be properly managed.

fields.title: AI Vision Analysis — Every Image Gets a Deep Look
fields.description: Upload an image anywhere in WLJ and the AI will comprehensively analyze it — identifying objects, reading text, describing the scene, and extracting actionable insights. Works in AI chat, camera scan, notes (new image upload!), inventory photos, and more. Your Chief of Staff now has visual context from recent images, so it can reference what you've scanned or photographed when giving advice.

fields.title: Notes — Your Personal Memory Layer
fields.description: A new Notes module is now available for capturing thoughts, ideas, and reference notes. Notes support color coding, pinning, tagging, full-text search with highlighted results, and semantic search powered by AI. Attach notes to any entity (tasks, goals, journal entries) and find them instantly with intelligent ranking.

fields.title: Your Chief of Staff is Faster, Smarter, and More Reliable
fields.description: Your Chief of Staff got a major quality-of-life upgrade. CoS now responds noticeably faster — we eliminated redundant database queries and moved background processing out of the response path. Calendar and task times are now displayed in your local timezone (no more UTC confusion). When you ask about your day or tasks, CoS always gives you the full briefing with your actual data — never generic advice. The chat also pre-warms the server when you open it, so you're less likely to see 'could not find server' after idle periods. If the server is cold, the chat silently retries once before showing an error.

fields.title: Journal Dashboard: Mood & Prompt Widgets Now Working
fields.description: The Journal home page got a major refresh. The 'Mood This Week' widget now correctly shows all the emotions you've selected across your entries — displayed as emoji + name (e.g., '😊 Great') so you can easily identify each one. Hover over any emotion for its full name. The 'Today's Prompt' widget now shows a daily rotating writing prompt based on your preferences. Mood and entry counts are now accurately calculated based on your entry dates.

fields.title: Smarter CoS: Better Context, Reasoning & Session Awareness
fields.description: Your Chief of Staff just got a major intelligence upgrade. CoS now has a much larger conversation memory (40 messages vs 15), tracks your page navigation to understand what you're doing, and thinks through context before responding — so when you're reading scripture and ask about the Sabbath, it talks about scripture, not your work routines. CoS also detects whether you're asking about what's on your screen vs. continuing an earlier topic. Intent recognition is now powered by GPT-4o for better understanding of what you mean. NEW: CoS now has long-term memory — it stores past conversations with semantic search, so it can naturally reference things you discussed days or weeks ago ('You mentioned last week...'). It also validates its own responses before sending them, and will automatically self-correct if it detects a context mismatch.

fields.title: CoS Tracks Everything on Your Calendar
fields.description: Your Chief of Staff now monitors and prompts on every type of calendar event — habits, goals, milestones, life events, and manual entries — not just tasks. CoS will prompt you before activities start, check in afterwards, and record your reflections. When you complete a habit, goal, or milestone (either through CoS or the app), it syncs across your calendar automatically. Clicking any calendar event now takes you directly to its edit page. The task form has also been reordered for a more natural flow: What → Notes → Recurring → Dates → Time.

fields.title: Daily Routine Tasks with CoS Check-ins
fields.description: Your daily routines (Quiet Time, Workout, etc.) can now be set up as recurring tasks with scheduled times. Tell CoS 'Add Quiet Time at 5:30am daily' and it will create a completable task that shows up on your calendar at the right time. CoS will prompt you before your routine starts, check in afterwards to ask how it went, and remember your reflections for future conversations. Your executive briefing now shows which routines you've completed and which are still pending.

fields.title: Capture: iOS Audio Downloads & Readable Transcripts
fields.description: Two improvements to Capture recordings: (1) The 'Save to Device' and 'Download Audio' buttons now work correctly in the iOS app — tap to save your recording to Files, AirDrop it, or share to other apps. (2) Full transcripts are now formatted with paragraph breaks at natural topic changes, making long transcripts much easier to read. No wording is changed — just cleaner formatting.

fields.title: Capture: Broader Audio Format Support
fields.description: The Capture feature now accepts a wider range of audio formats including MP4, OGG, and CAF files. This fixes an issue where recordings saved from iOS devices (which use the MP4 format) couldn't be re-uploaded via the Upload Audio File option. Downloaded recordings now also save with the correct audio extension (.m4a instead of .mp4) so your device recognizes them as audio files.

fields.title: Clickable Calendar Events
fields.description: Calendar events in the Time Command Center are now clickable. Tap any event to take action: task-linked events open the task editor, goal-linked events go to the goal page, habit-linked events go to the habit page, and manually created events open an edit form where you can update details or delete the event — all without leaving the calendar.

fields.title: Chief of Staff v2: Your Intelligent Daily Partner
fields.description: A major upgrade to your Chief of Staff. It now proactively checks in before and after your activities, learns from your reflections over time, detects patterns in your well-being (like workout fatigue or consistency drops), and suggests goals when the evidence supports them. Events are intelligently prioritized — low-priority items auto-shift around conflicts while important ones stay put. The tone adapts to your day: encouraging when you're on a streak, empathetic when things are tough, and energized before workouts. All of this runs behind the scenes with a feature flag — opt in when you're ready.

fields.title: Smart Conflict Detection for Your Calendar
fields.description: Your Chief of Staff now checks for scheduling conflicts before creating or moving events. If a time overlap is detected, you'll see exactly which events conflict and get suggested alternative time slots. Protected events like Workouts, Bible Study, Prayer, and Health appointments are automatically flagged, so your most important commitments stay safe. You always have the final say — override, reschedule, or cancel.

fields.title: Full Calendar Control via Your Chief of Staff
fields.description: Your Chief of Staff can now manage your entire calendar through conversation. Ask things like 'move my Wednesday meeting to Thursday', 'cancel my 2pm appointment', or 'what's on my calendar this week?' — and it handles the rest. Updates, reschedules, and cancellations are all tracked in your schedule history so nothing is ever lost.

fields.title: Sharper, More Precise Guidance
fields.description: Your Chief of Staff now double-checks every response before you see it, ensuring you always get clear, natural guidance without any technical jargon slipping through. If something doesn't meet quality standards, it's automatically corrected before delivery. The system also tracks its own accuracy over time and alerts the team if anything needs attention.

fields.title: Improved Reliability & Graceful Recovery
fields.description: Behind the scenes, your Chief of Staff is now more resilient. If something hiccups — a slow connection, a brief service interruption — the system handles it gracefully and keeps your data safe. You'll see a friendly status message instead of an error, and everything catches up automatically. Your commitments and schedule are always protected, even when things aren't running at full speed.

fields.title: Proactive Schedule Protection & Deadline Alerts
fields.description: Your Chief of Staff now watches your schedule and commitments proactively. When your load gets heavy, you'll receive specific recommendations — like blocking time for what matters most, adjusting deadlines before they become emergencies, or focusing on the most urgent items when deadlines converge. You'll also get timely reminders at 24 hours, 4 hours, and 1 hour before commitment deadlines, with easy options to confirm your plan, adjust, or close. Everything is advisory — your schedule is never changed without your say-so.

fields.title: Persistent Accountability & Recovery Tracking
fields.description: Your Chief of Staff now remembers your accountability level across conversations — no more silent resets. If you've been drifting, the system maintains appropriate follow-up intensity until you demonstrate sustained improvement: 7 clean days, at least 3 honored commitments, and zero missed priorities. A new behavioral trend tracker monitors whether each area of your life is improving, stable, or declining over time.

fields.title: Smarter Time & Deadline Intelligence
fields.description: Your Chief of Staff now requires specific times for commitments — no more silent assumptions. When you say 'I'll finish this today', it will ask 'by when specifically?' to ensure accountability is precise. A new deadline surfacing engine proactively tracks everything due in the next 24 hours, 3 days, and 7 days, with collision detection when deadlines bunch up. Protected blocks (like morning prayer) now have graduated resistance — the system will explain the conflict and suggest alternatives before allowing an override. Timezone changes automatically preserve your intended times.

fields.title: Learning Mode & Priority System
fields.description: Your Chief of Staff can now enter Learning Mode — a dedicated listening state where it learns your priorities, values, and preferences without taking any actions. A new priority weighting system lets you declare what matters most (non-negotiable, important, or flexible), and the CoS will gently hold you accountable when your behavior drifts from your declared priorities. You can also track partial progress on tasks with a progress slider.

fields.title: Financial Command Center — Full Suite
fields.description: The Owner Financial Command Center is now fully built out with 7 pages: interactive daily cost charts, per-call audit ledger with filtering, CSV data export, per-user deep-dive diagnostics, a what-if scenario simulator for cost/revenue projections, and budget guardrail monitoring with visual progress bars. All LLM call sites across the app now report cost telemetry automatically.

fields.title: Smarter, Faster Chief of Staff Responses
fields.description: Your Chief of Staff now adapts its response length to match your question — short questions get short answers, complex analysis gets the detail it deserves. A new 'Response Detail Level' setting in Settings lets you choose between Concise, Balanced, Strategic, or Deep Dive styles. Behind the scenes, responses are more reliable with automatic retry on temporary connection issues, and token usage is now tracked for every conversation.

fields.title: Full Engine Execution Authority — Synthetic Mode
fields.description: All nine intelligence engines now have Execute buttons in the Ops Command Center. Context-dependent engines (UAL, SAE, PIE, PRIE, ICQG) run in Synthetic Batch Evaluation Mode — iterating all active users and re-evaluating current system state using each engine's existing logic. No fake events are created and no raw data is altered. Synthetic engines are clearly marked with a purple 'Synthetic' badge and descriptive tooltip. This extends the manual execution capability from 4 batch-native engines to the full intelligence pipeline.

fields.title: Per-Engine Manual Execution Controls
fields.description: Individual intelligence engines can now be triggered manually from the Ops Command Center. Each engine card for DBE, WIRE, DNE, and PGE now has an 'Execute' button that queues the engine for immediate background execution via Celery, with real-time status feedback showing queued, running, and completed states with execution duration. Includes idempotency guards to prevent duplicate runs, freeze detection for disabled engines, and full audit logging. This also fixes an existing issue where engine re-run buttons could fail for certain engines.

fields.title: SAME Manual Execution Control
